tracks.legalName: Conviction Expungement, first-time drug offender, HRS § 706-622.5(4)

controllingAuthority.summary: Two stages, both settled. Stage one is a written motion in the participant's own existing penal case, filed in the court that sentenced or convicted them, seeking a court order expunging the record of conviction; stage two is the HCJDC 159(b) Expungement Application submitted to the Hawaii Criminal Justice Data Center with a copy of that order attached. The stage-one vehicle is fixed by Haw. R. Penal P. 47(a), which provides that "An application to the court for an order shall be by motion", so Hawaii penal practice does not distinguish an application from a motion however the statute words it; the Rules of Penal Procedure govern because Rule 54(a) applies them to all penal proceedings and none of these provisions supplies its own procedure. Mandatory. 'the court shall issue a court order to expunge'. The proviso states conditions, not a discretion. The court has no listed ground to refuse a qualifying application. No official statewide Hawaii Judiciary expungement form exists for stage one in any circuit, so a controlled custom pleading is permitted and is the only available strategy. Venue follows the offence and is a participant input rather than a track constant. Nothing here makes the Hawaii implementation ready.

components.notes: Stage one, and no longer blocked. A written motion under Haw. R. Penal P. 47(a), in the participant's own existing penal case, seeking an order expunging the record of conviction under HRS 706-622.5(4). It states the grounds and the relief sought, is accompanied by a memorandum where it involves a question of law, is supported by a Haw. R. Penal P. 47(d) declaration for facts not appearing of record, and carries a Rule 49(c) certificate of service on the prosecuting attorney. It is noticed for hearing under Rule 47(a) and Rule 45(c) unless presented ex parte. Required allegations: (1) The participant's identity and the criminal case: court, circuit, case number, offence and statute section, and date of judgment. (2) That the person was sentenced to probation under HRS 706-622.5. (3) That the person successfully completed the substance abuse treatment programme. (4) That the person complied with the other terms and conditions of probation. The Hawaii Supreme Court has held that a person who completed the probation term and was discharged, and so satisfied the disposition of the court under HRS 706-630, has in effect complied with the terms and conditions of probation for purposes of subsection (4): 129 H. 363, 300 P.3d 1022 (2013), printed in the case notes to the section. (5) That the person had not previously been sentenced under HRS 706-622.5 at the time of the sentence in question, which is what makes the one-time eligibility available. (6) That the person has not previously been granted an expungement of conviction under HRS 706-622.5 or HRS 706-622.8 — the bar in HRS 706-622.8 runs both ways. (7) The specific offence for which expungement is sought. The order reaches 'that particular offense', so the motion must identify it rather than the case as a whole. (8) The relief sought: a court order expunging the record of conviction for that offence. No official statewide Judiciary form exists, so this is a controlled custom pleading and there is no officialFormId to bind.

The order expunging the record of conviction, lodged with the stage-one motion. No statute requires the movant to lodge one and no penal rule read here does either, but it is a required component on practical and procedural grounds: every one of the five provisions operates through an order the court issues, Rule 7(f)(3) of the Rules of the Circuit Courts compels a proposed order where the motion is presented ex parte, and stage two cannot begin without it because the Data Center requires a copy of the Order Granting the Expungement of Conviction to accompany the HCJDC 159(b) application. A participant who leaves the courthouse with a granted motion and no signed order cannot proceed.

rules.filing: Stage one: file a written motion in the existing penal case, in the court that entered the judgment. Stage two: submit the HCJDC 159(b) Expungement Application to the Hawaii Criminal Justice Data Center with a copy of the signed order attached.
rules.fees: No fee is prescribed by the statute on any of the five stage-one routes, and the Judiciary publishes no filing fee for a motion filed in an existing penal case. What remains open is clerk cost practice, which is recorded as a release-level question rather than answered here. An HCJDC application fee applies at stage two.
rules.feeWaiver: None arises from the statute. Haw. R. Penal P. Form B, the Request to Proceed Without Paying Filing Fees, is the companion to the Rule 40 post-conviction petition and is not a component of an expungement packet.
rules.notice: No statutory notice. Not one of the five provisions requires notice to the prosecuting attorney, to a victim, to the Attorney General, to the Data Center or to any agency. The notice that exists is the service every filed document receives.
rules.service: Haw. R. Penal P. 49(a): all written submissions to the court shall be served upon each of the parties promptly after filing. The prosecuting attorney is a party to the underlying penal case and is served under that rule. Proof of service is required by Haw. R. Penal P. 49(c), so a certificate of service is part of the stage-one filing.
rules.participantSignature: The participant signs the motion personally, and signs the Haw. R. Penal P. 47(d) declaration.
rules.notarization: None. Haw. R. Penal P. 47(d) permits an unsworn declaration in lieu of an affidavit, subscribed as true under penalty of law and dated, which removes any notarization requirement from the stage-one filing.

stageOne.vehicleBasis: Haw. R. Penal P. 47(a): "An application to the court for an order shall be by motion. A motion other than one made during a trial or hearing shall be in writing unless the court permits it to be made orally. It shall state the grounds upon which it is made and shall set forth the relief or order sought. A motion involving a question of law shall be accompanied by a memorandum in support of the motion. If a motion requires the consideration of facts not appearing of record, it shall be supported by affidavit or declaration."
stageOne.rulesApply: Haw. R. Penal P. 54(a) applies the Rules of Penal Procedure to all penal proceedings in all courts of the State, and Rule 54(b)'s exception for statutory proceedings with their own procedure does not bite because none of the five provisions supplies one. Rule 54(d) makes the Rules of Penal Procedure govern over the Rules of the Circuit Courts and the Rules of the District Courts in any conflict.
stageOne.filingActor: The person sentenced under this part, or a probation officer. The statute names both. A packet is built for the person; the probation-officer route is not a LegalEase output and should be named in the copy so a participant whose probation officer has already applied does not file a second time.

controllingAuthority.summary: Two stages, both settled. components.notes: Stage one, and no longer blocked. A written motion under Haw. R. Penal P. 47(a), in the participant's own existing penal case, seeking an order expunging the record of conviction under HRS 706-622.5(5). It states the grounds and the relief sought, is accompanied by a memorandum where it involves a question of law, is supported by a Haw. R. Penal P. 47(d) declaration for facts not appearing of record, and carries a Rule 49(c) certificate of service on the prosecuting attorney. It is noticed for hearing under Rule 47(a) and Rule 45(c) unless presented ex parte. Required allegations: (1) The participant's identity and the criminal case: court, circuit, case number and date of judgment. (2) That the conviction was under HRS 712-1249 for possession of marijuana. (3) That the amount possessed, as convicted, was three grams or less. (4) That the set of facts and circumstances giving rise to the conviction resulted in no other criminal charge. No official statewide Judiciary form exists, so this is a controlled custom pleading and there is no officialFormId to bind.

legalDesignDecision.rationale: Both stages are now reconciled against primary authority and the stage-one build blocker is closed. The vehicle is a written motion under Haw. R. Penal P. 47(a), which resolves the application-versus-motion question the memo carried since normalization: Rule 47(a) provides in terms that an application to the court for an order shall be by motion, so the statutory word does not change the instrument. The Rules of Penal Procedure govern because Rule 54(a) applies them to all penal proceedings and no expungement provision supplies its own procedure. No official statewide Judiciary expungement form exists in any circuit, which was established from the Judiciary's own published form inventory rather than from a failed search, so a controlled custom pleading is permitted and is the only available strategy; the content is prescribed by the statute and by Rule 47, so a generated motion has a specification to be audited against and nothing is invented. Service is Rule 49(a) on the prosecuting attorney as a party, with Rule 49(c) proof; there is no statutory notice and no statutory hearing, and the motion is designed as a noticed motion under Rule 47(a) and Rule 45(c). A proposed order is a required component because the order is the operative instrument and stage two cannot start without a copy of it. Stage two is one document, HCJDC 159(b) at REV-2026-06-03, and the two identity keys the repository formerly carried have been collapsed to it. What is settled is the design; the implementation is not ready and nothing here makes it so.

components.notes: Stage one, and no longer blocked. A written motion under Haw. R. Penal P. 47(a), in the participant's own existing penal case, seeking an order expunging the record of conviction under HRS 291E-64(e). It states the grounds and the relief sought, is accompanied by a memorandum where it involves a question of law, is supported by a Haw. R. Penal P. 47(d) declaration for facts not appearing of record, and carries a Rule 49(c) certificate of service on the prosecuting attorney. It is noticed for hearing under Rule 47(a) and Rule 45(c) unless presented ex parte. Required allegations: (1) Identity and the criminal case: court, circuit, case number and date of judgment. (2) That the conviction was of a first-time violation under HRS 291E-64(b)(1), or under HRS 291-4.3 as it existed before Act 189, Session Laws of Hawaii 2000. (3) That the person had no prior alcohol enforcement contacts. HRS 291E-64(c) provides that any conviction or plea under the section is itself a prior alcohol enforcement contact. (4) That the person has attained the age of twenty-one. (5) That the person has fulfilled the terms of the sentence imposed by the court. (6) That the person has had no subsequent alcohol or drug related enforcement contacts. (7) That the person was not in possession of a commercial learner's permit or commercial driver's licence, and was not convicted in a commercial motor vehicle or while transporting hazardous materials. (8) The relief sought: an expungement order. No official statewide Judiciary form exists, so this is a controlled custom pleading and there is no officialFormId to bind.

legalDesignDecision.rationale: Both stages are now reconciled against primary authority and the stage-one build blocker is closed. The vehicle is a written motion under Haw. R. Penal P. 47(a), which resolves the application-versus-motion question the memo carried since normalization: Rule 47(a) provides in terms that an application to the court for an order shall be by motion, so the statutory word does not change the instrument. The Rules of Penal Procedure govern because Rule 54(a) applies them to all penal proceedings and no expungement provision supplies its own procedure. No official statewide Judiciary expungement form exists in any circuit, which was established from the Judiciary's own published form inventory rather than from a failed search, so a controlled custom pleading is permitted and is the only available strategy; the content is prescribed by the statute and by Rule 47, so a generated motion has a specification to be audited against and nothing is invented. Service is Rule 49(a) on the prosecuting attorney as a party, with Rule 49(c) proof; there is no statutory notice and no statutory hearing, and the motion is designed as a noticed motion under Rule 47(a) and Rule 45(c). A proposed order is a required component because the order is the operative instrument and stage two cannot start without a copy of it. Stage two is one document, HCJDC 159(b) at REV-2026-06-03, and the two identity keys the repository formerly carried have been collapsed to it. What is settled is the design; the implementation is not ready and nothing here makes it so.
